analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's BTOS series asks construction firms, NAICS 23, whether they used AI in the last two weeks. The latest reading is 16.0%, compared with 14.3% in the prior period. That is the only direct adoption measure in the material.

Per BuiltWorlds, the construction technology research network tracks site robotics, jobsite IoT, and digital preconstruction across research programs and member benchmarking. Its Buildings Conference places specific emphasis on data centers and AI infrastructure, and its AI/ML Conference covers use cases across construction, building, and operation, implementation strategies, and case studies. The coverage summary for this sector lists computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning among the areas sourced from AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers. Per AGC, the association surveys technology adoption and safety-technology compliance across US builders.

Per CREtech, construction companies are among the leaders converging at its New York real estate AI conference, which advertises 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and 20,000+ pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings. Its sponsors and partners represent companies shaping real estate in the age of AI, and startups attend. Per CREtech and MetaProp, venture flow across architecture, engineering, and construction technology is tracked alongside property tech. No dollar figures are given in the excerpts.

Per AGC, contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and construction unemployment hit a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill openings. Construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026. These conditions appear in the same association survey material but are not tied to AI adoption in the excerpts.

The excerpts do not report ROI evidence. BuiltWorlds mentions case studies and lessons learned from specific solutions, but no measured returns are stated. Risks and regulatory posture are not addressed directly. AGC's work includes safety-technology compliance, but no specific rules or risk findings are cited.

A reader deciding whether to deploy should treat the Census Bureau's 16.0% as the hard adoption baseline, up from 14.3%, and use BuiltWorlds, AGC, and CREtech channels for case-level and vendor detail. The material here does not yet provide ROI or risk benchmarks, so deployment decisions would need evidence beyond these excerpts.

https://cretech.com/.brief: According to the page, CREtech New York 2026 will be held at the Javits Center in New York City on October 20, 21, 2026, and will bring together 3,000 leaders, 150 speakers, and more than 20,000 pre-scheduled 1:1 meetings. The event is described as a leading real-estate AI conference where sessions are led by operators actively deploying AI in their portfolios, offering real strategy rather than theory. The conference aims to connect owners, developers, investors, occupiers, construction firms, brokers, and tech leaders to discuss AI’s impact on real-estate assets. Tickets are limited, and sponsors and partners are said to represent companies shaping the future of real-estate in the age of AI.

https://www.agc.org/.brief: The Associated General Contractors of America reports having over 27,000 member firms. According to an association survey, construction input costs climbed 8.9% between August 2025 and August 2026, with war and tariff impacts disrupting projects. The association also states contractors added 22,000 jobs in August and the construction unemployment rate hit a record low of 3.1%, while firms struggle to fill openings. The page promotes a safety conference in San Diego and a leadership course for project executives.

https://builtworlds.com/.brief: BuiltWorlds operates a membership network for buildings and infrastructure professionals. The organization hosts an annual Buildings Conference addressing innovation in building development, design, materials and systems, with particular focus on data centers and AI infrastructure. It also runs an annual AI/ML Conference exploring artificial intelligence and machine learning adoption across the architecture, engineering, construction and operations industry, covering implementation strategies, use cases, and lessons learned from companies deploying these technologies.
